classification.difficultyReason: Select two connecting vectors without part scaffolding, translate the midpoint and division ratio into vector multiples, and compare them to prove collinearity.

content.prompt:
OAB is a triangle.

A is the midpoint of OC.

N is the midpoint of AB.

M is on OB such that $OM:MB=2:1$.

$\overrightarrow{NB}=\underset{\sim}{x},\quad\overrightarrow{OA}=\underset{\sim}{y}$.

Prove that MNC is a straight line.

spec.description: OC is horizontal with A its midpoint. Triangle OAB has N at the midpoint of AB and M two-thirds of the way from O to B. Only OC, OB and AB are drawn; the proposed line MNC is absent.
spec.mathematics: OA=AC; AN=NB; OM:MB=2:1. All six point labels and both marked interior points are retained.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent question figure; no proof vectors or proposed collinear line are supplied.

answer.short: $\overrightarrow{MN}=-\frac13(\underset{\sim}{x}-\underset{\sim}{y})$ and $\overrightarrow{MC}=-\frac43(\underset{\sim}{x}-\underset{\sim}{y})=4\overrightarrow{MN}$. These vectors are parallel and share M, so M, N and C are collinear.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\overrightarrow{AB}&=2\underset{\sim}{x}\\\overrightarrow{OB}&=\overrightarrow{OA}+\overrightarrow{AB}\\\overrightarrow{OB}&=\underset{\sim}{y}+2\underset{\sim}{x}\\\overrightarrow{MN}&=\overrightarrow{MB}+\overrightarrow{BN}\\\overrightarrow{MN}&=\frac13(2\underset{\sim}{x}+\underset{\sim}{y})-\underset{\sim}{x}\\\overrightarrow{MN}&=-\frac13(\underset{\sim}{x}-\underset{\sim}{y})\\\overrightarrow{MC}&=\overrightarrow{MO}+\overrightarrow{OC}\\\overrightarrow{MC}&=-\frac23(2\underset{\sim}{x}+\underset{\sim}{y})+2\underset{\sim}{y}\\\overrightarrow{MC}&=-\frac43\underset{\sim}{x}+\frac43\underset{\sim}{y}\\\overrightarrow{MC}&=-\frac43(\underset{\sim}{x}-\underset{\sim}{y})\\\overrightarrow{MC}&=4\overrightarrow{MN}\end{aligned}$$
The vectors $\overrightarrow{MN}$ and $\overrightarrow{MC}$ are parallel and share the common point M. Therefore M, N and C lie on a straight line.
